findings: All six opted-in classes use plain JUnit. No Spring extension or MockitoBean lifecycle is enrolled.
Creation listener starts in BeforeEachCallback, after BeforeAll; all six fixtures create method-owned mocks synchronously in BeforeEach or the test body.
Exact-runtime Mockito bytecode confirms listener registration/removal uses thread-local MockingProgress and clearInlineMock(object) calls single-object clearMock, not clearAllMocks.
ExtensionContext stores one Scope per test invocation; removal plus finally clearing the owned list releases scope references.
AfterEachCallback runs after user AfterEach cleanup; LearnerProjectionMemoizationTest retains its transaction completion and synchronization teardown before mock disposal.

Bound shared spy is not acquired by the per-method listener. clearInvocations only removes its per-case history and preserves its identity and stubs. Its clearInlineMock is explicit in its class owner AfterAll.
Bound SAME_THREAD is appropriate because its committedConfigs, real catalogs and spy are shared mutable class fixtures and pathResolutionCalls reads invocation history.
All six AfterAll callbacks release only their explicit static fields; committedConfigs is cleared. No global Mockito cleanup or Spring context eviction is introduced.

Current root Memoization functional assertion remains byte-preserved below the lifecycle-only hunks. No assertion, production source, SRS test, build option, heap setting, fork setting or selector is changed.

Private validation probes additionally exercise two concurrent owners, foreign stub preservation, BeforeEach/body failure cleanup, listener reuse, and the same real Spring context across the six plain fixtures.
limits: This opt-in extension only owns mocks created on its test execution thread after its BeforeEach callback. Constructors, BeforeAll, asynchronous workers, static mocks and future Spring fixture integration require separate explicit ownership.
The existing SRS metrics MockitoBean returns null to BackgroundMetricsTask after scheduler wakeups. Its logged background NPE is unrelated to the SQL assertions and heap ownership correction.
The 1536m sequence with forced GC only between classes measures retained class-lifecycle heap and preservation; it does not establish full 3201-test or remote-CI acceptance.
